Introduction

A Residential Service Agency (RSA) in Maryland provides non-medical home care services. The MD Department of Health — Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ) oversees RSA licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Maryland’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Maryland’s Regulations

OHCQ licenses RSAs under COMAR regulations. Requirements include state licensing, background checks, training standards, and quality monitoring.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

RSAs provide personal care, homemaker services, companion care, and respite services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the MD SDAT, obtain an EIN, apply for RSA license through OHCQ, and secure required insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Maryland benchmarks: Private pay rates $22-$32/hour, Medicaid rates $18-$25/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, technology systems, and quality monitoring tools.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

Maryland requires background checks and competency-based training for all direct care workers.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop comprehensive policies meeting OHCQ requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Partner with healthcare systems, Area Agencies on Aging, and community organizations in the Baltimore-Washington corridor.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing, training records, and quality improvement programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

What is an RSA? A Residential Service Agency provides non-medical personal care and support services in clients’ homes.
